editorialHook: November fog is rolling in soft and slow, and SF is countering with a week so packed with music, coffee, and good vibes that you honestly have no excuse to stay on the couch.

picks.d: Ten years of caffeination at Fort Mason and they are not slowing down. Dozens of specialty roasters, live bands, tea nerds welcome too, and unlimited samplings for $29 is genuinely one of the best deals of the season. Grab your most coffee-obsessed friend and make a full morning of it by the water.

picks.t: Brand New at Bill Graham Civic
picks.d: If you know, you know. Brand New is one of the most beloved and historically elusive bands in emo and post-hardcore, and any appearance is a genuine event. Bill Graham Civic Auditorium is the perfect room for their dense, layered guitar work and heavy introspective energy. Do not sleep on this one.

One of the original UK punk bands is celebrating 50 years and calling it a farewell tour, which makes this a certified bucket-list moment for punk and goth fans. The Fillmore is an iconic room for a show this historically significant. If you have ever even casually liked punk music, go.

picks.t: Olafur Arnalds at the Castro Theater
picks.d: The Icelandic sound artist who blends neo-classical piano and strings with lush electronic textures is doing two nights at the Castro, which is honestly the most perfectly matched venue-artist pairing imaginable. His live show is a full sensory experience that feels more like stepping into a film than attending a concert. A genuinely special way to spend an evening.

picks.t: Dirtybird Night Market at Thrive City
picks.d: Free DJ sets, vendors, games, and cocktails right outside Chase Center on a Friday evening. This is the perfect low-commitment start to the weekend where you can grab a drink, dance a little, shop a little, and see where the night takes you. Bring friends or go solo and make some.

SYML performing his Solo in North America tour inside the ornate Castro Theatre is one of those rare venue-and-artist combinations that feels almost too perfect. His cinematic, emotionally atmospheric indie folk hits differently in a room with that much history and character. A quietly stunning Friday night option.

A whole festival dedicated entirely to cider at SPARK Social SF in Mission Bay, which is exactly the kind of very good idea that belongs in November. The outdoor setting is lively, the vibes are autumnal, and you will almost certainly discover a new favorite. 21+ and very much worth the afternoon.

picks.t: Foy Vance at Great American Music Hall
picks.d: The Irish singer-songwriter with one of the most deeply soulful voices in folk and blues is playing one of SF's most beautiful historic rooms, joined by Bonnie Bishop and Ryan McMullan. This triple bill is a rare treat and the ornate GAMH interior makes everything feel more special. A perfect Sunday evening.

Food, local vendors, and a Friday evening by the waterfront at Fort Mason. Free to attend and the views alone are worth showing up for. A lovely and very San Francisco way to ease into the weekend before things get louder elsewhere.

picks.t: Russian Circles w/ Primitive Man at GAMH
picks.d: The Chicago post-metal trio who do crushing, all-instrumental heaviness are playing the Great American Music Hall with doom-metal bruisers Primitive Man opening. This is one of the most intense and well-curated double bills of the whole week. Tickets are $30 advance and absolutely worth every dollar.

picks.t: Exploratorium After Dark: Unplug and Play
picks.d: The Exploratorium opens its doors after hours for adults only and this month the theme is unplugging and playing, which sounds like a genuinely fun and different way to spend a Thursday. 18+ only, and it hits differently when the kids are not around. Great solo or group option.

picks.t: de Young Museum - Free Admission Weekend
picks.d: Bank of America Museums on Us means Bay Area residents get into the de Young for free this Saturday and Sunday. The permanent collection alone is worth the trip, and Golden Gate Park in November has a whole moody, beautiful thing going on. A completely free and genuinely lovely way to spend a weekend morning.

picks.t: ACT - John Proctor Is the Villain (Opens!)
picks.d: Kimberly Belflower's Tony-nominated play gets its West Coast premiere at ACT's Toni Rembe Theater, directed by Jess McLeod in collaboration with Seattle Rep and Center Theatre Group. It follows a high school class reading The Crucible and asking very sharp questions about who the story is really about. Opening night energy is always electric.

ongoing.t: Dear San Francisco at Club Fugazi
ongoing.d: Circus meets SF history in an immersive acrobatics and storytelling show running all week in North Beach.

ongoing.t: SF Playhouse: Peter Pan Goes Wrong
ongoing.d: The beloved comedy runs through November 28 at the intimate 199-seat theater on Post St.

ongoing.t: SFMOMA: RM x SFMOMA - Between You and Me
ongoing.d: The BTS leader's collection of Korean modernists alongside SFMOMA's own works, ongoing through 2027.
Monumental hemp-cloth paintings filling the galleries on Larkin St, open Tue-Sun.

ongoing.t: Minnesota Street Project: Raymond Meeks - Assemblage
ongoing.d: Free photography show at Casemore Gallery through November 14.

new.name: Bare Bones
new.d: Three restaurant-world friends opening a counter-service rotisserie chicken spot on Taraval, one of fall 2026's most anticipated debuts.

new.name: Scout
new.d: Neighborhood pasta and pizza concept landing on Chestnut St just in time for cozy season.

new.name: Stir Crazy
new.d: Longtime Mezcalito bartender Jacob Morris opens his first solo project with thoughtfully made classics in the old Black Magic Voodoo Lounge space.

new.name: Bayview Oyster Bar
new.d: Fresh oysters and Louisiana-Bay Area fusion from April Spears, part of an exciting new dining cluster on Third St.

new.name: Bar Antoine Lounge
new.d: A 22-year-old bar director opens an 80-seat lounge at the Galleria Park Hotel with clever bites and serious cocktails.

new.name: Ah Ma's Kitchen
new.d: Yelp's Best New Restaurant of 2026 is on Clement St and serving Hong Kong flavors with a creative twist.

classic.name: RT Bistro
classic.d: One of the most buzzed-about new restaurants of 2026, earning serious praise from locals all fall.

classic.name: La Cigale
classic.d: No tips, no reservations, just excellent wood-fired food and a refreshingly unpretentious neighborhood vibe.

classic.name: Khao Tiew
classic.d: Walk-in-only Thai spot with a devoted following and the kind of food people rearrange their nights for.

classic.name: Banh Mi A Mui
classic.d: The spiritual successor to the beloved Sing Sing, bringing serious banh mi craft back to the neighborhood.

bars.name: Stir Crazy
bars.d: Jacob Morris brings his years behind the stick at Mezcalito to his very own corner of Lombard St.

bars.name: Bar Antoine Lounge
bars.d: Dark wood, velvet armchairs, clever food, and serious craft cocktails on the mezzanine of the Galleria Park Hotel.

bars.name: Bar Part Time
bars.d: The Mission natural wine bar known for good pours and legendary late-night dance raves.

bars.name: Dalva
bars.d: One of the Mission's most reliable bars for well-made drinks and a crowd that actually wants to be there.

bars.name: Blackbird
bars.d: Beloved Castro neighborhood bar hosting the Gay Men Speed Dating event Saturday and always worth a visit.

bars.name: Mezcalito
bars.d: The Polk St favorite that trained the guy who just opened Stir Crazy. High bar. The mezcal selection is excellent.

bars.name: Halcyon SF
bars.d: Early 1900s brick and steel warehouse turned elegant nightclub, hosting FOVOS on Saturday.

bars.name: 1015 Folsom
bars.d: SF's premier electronic music venue with Main Phase bringing UK garage and breaks on Friday.

games.teams: Golden State Warriors vs. Orlando Magic
games.detail: Home game with new local Bay Area food and beverage lineup to try at the arena.

sports.note: The Golden State Valkyries are your 2026 WNBA Champions! Their parade already happened on Nov 4 but the city is still celebrating.

concerts.d: Intimate, cinematic indie folk in the ornate Castro Theatre as part of his Solo in North America tour. If atmospheric, emotionally rich songwriting is your thing, this is a perfect Friday.
Grammy-winning powerhouse vocalist and storyteller performing in SF on Saturday night. Her live shows are consistently called transcendent and that is not an exaggeration.
Canadian singer-songwriter Afie Jurvanen brings his lush, jazz-tinged indie folk to August Hall. Cool, sophisticated, and effortlessly listenable.

concerts.t: Foy Vance w/ Bonnie Bishop and Ryan McMullan
concerts.d: A triple bill of deeply soulful folk and blues at one of SF's most beautiful rooms. Doors at 6pm so get there early and soak in the GAMH interior.
The R&B and soul breakout of the decade brings his raspy, emotive vocals to Chase Center. Big room, big voice, big night.
Any Brand New show is a rare and significant event. Dense guitar work, introspective lyrics, and a room full of people who have waited years for this.
Fifty years of punk history on stage at the Fillmore on a farewell tour. Genuinely historic. Go tell your friends right now.
The ex-At the Drive-In post-hardcore outfit playing the intimate Rickshaw Stop is exactly as good as it sounds. Angular, intense, emotionally charged. $20 advance.
Reverb-drenched indie rock anthems like The Funeral in the intimate Regency Ballroom. The 1,400-cap room makes this a rare chance to see them up close.
All-instrumental post-metal heaviness at GAMH with one of doom metal's most crushing openers. $30 advance for a double bill this good is a steal.

concertsOngoing.t: SF Symphony: Isabel Leonard Sings Ravel
concertsOngoing.d: Runs Friday Nov 6 at 7:30pm and Sunday Nov 8 at 2pm at Davies Symphony Hall.

concertsOngoing.t: SF Opera: The Marriage of Figaro
concertsOngoing.d: Mozart's classic running through the month at the War Memorial Opera House, from $30.
Friday Nov 6 at 7:30pm at the War Memorial Opera House, from $30.

singles.t: SF Singles Speed Dating Game Night
singles.d: Speed dating at a cocktail bar with a game night twist, which immediately makes the whole thing less intimidating and more fun. Iron Horse Cocktails is a solid venue and the game format gives you something to talk about besides the usual opener questions.

singles.t: SF Singles Speed Dating Ages 22-30 at Coffee Shop
singles.d: A daytime low-key speed dating session for younger singles at Sunset Commons, which is genuinely the least stressful format for meeting people. Start with structured speed dating then hang out and talk freely afterward. Afternoon coffee-shop energy only.

singles.t: Gay Men Speed Dating at Blackbird
singles.d: Dedicated speed dating night for gay men at the beloved Castro bar Blackbird. Pre-Dating Speed Dating runs these well and Blackbird is exactly the right kind of cozy neighborhood spot to make it feel comfortable rather than awkward.

Meet 8 to 12 local singles in one evening at the stylish Jay Hotel. A structured and efficient format that works especially well for busy professionals who want to actually meet people rather than swipe forever.

singles.t: Run Club SF - Weekly Group Runs
singles.d: If you can run a couple of miles at a 12-minute pace you are in, and they call themselves a social club with a running problem which tells you everything about the vibe. Tuesday in Golden Gate Park, Thursday at Kezar Stadium, Saturday mornings at rotating spots.

singles.t: SF Social Club November Happy Hour
singles.d: SF Social Club and Neighbourgood are combining their communities for drinks, conversation, and karaoke at Lost and Found SF. The kind of event where you show up not knowing anyone and leave with actual plans for the weekend.

singlesOngoing.t: November Project SF - Free Weekly Workouts
singlesOngoing.d: Multiple mornings per week at rotating SF locations. Radically inclusive, no sign-up, just show up.
Sundays at 10am from the Panhandle through Golden Gate Park, 2,599 members strong, all paces welcome.
Flag football, kickball, bocce, and more running through November across SF recreational spots.

date.title: Free Waterfront Friday
date.tagline: Night markets, fog, and good conversation - no wallet required.

steps.title: Fort Mason Night Market
steps.detail: Start at the Fort Mason Night Market for free food vendor browsing and waterfront views. The bay at dusk is doing its thing.

steps.title: Walk to Thrive City
steps.detail: Stroll or Lyft over to the Dirtybird Night Market at Thrive City Plaza near Chase Center. Also free, also great.

steps.title: Dance and Explore
steps.detail: Grab a cocktail from a vendor, check out the DJ sets, and let the evening go wherever it wants to go.

date.title: Coffee, Museum, and Something Cozy
date.tagline: A Saturday that starts slow and ends just right.

steps.title: SF Coffee Festival
steps.detail: Start your Saturday at Fort Mason for the 10th Annual SF Coffee Festival. $29 each for unlimited samplings and the vibe is very good.

steps.title: de Young Museum (Free!)
steps.detail: Walk or bike into Golden Gate Park and hit the de Young for free with Bank of America Museums on Us. The park in November is quietly beautiful.

steps.title: Dinner in the Neighborhood
steps.detail: Wind up the day at one of the new spots like Scout on Chestnut or Bar Antoine Lounge for cocktails and bites.

date.title: Show Night Done Right
date.tagline: An unforgettable evening of music and dinner in the city.

steps.title: Early Dinner at Ah Ma's Kitchen
steps.detail: Head to Clement St for Cantonese fusion at Yelp's Best New Restaurant of 2026. Book ahead.

steps.title: Olafur Arnalds at the Castro Theater
steps.detail: The Icelandic neo-classical artist's two-night run is the most atmospheric concert of the week. The Castro is a genuinely magical room for this.

steps.title: Nightcap at Bar Antoine Lounge
steps.detail: End at the Galleria Park Hotel mezzanine bar for a craft cocktail in those dark wood and velvet armchairs. Very good decision.

solo.title: Museum and Park Saturday
solo.tagline: Some of the best solo hours you can spend in this city cost nothing.

steps.title: de Young Museum
steps.detail: Free for Bay Area residents this weekend via Bank of America Museums on Us. Walk the galleries at your own pace with no one to compromise with.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Wander
steps.detail: November light in the park is genuinely gorgeous. No plan needed, just walk.

steps.title: Minnesota Street Project
steps.detail: Free galleries including Raymond Meeks: Assemblage through November 14. A quiet, interesting hour.

solo.title: Coffee Festival Solo Run
solo.tagline: No one to slow you down at the espresso bar.

steps.title: SF Coffee Festival Opens
steps.detail: Be there when Fort Mason opens. $29 for unlimited samplings and going solo means you can sprint between roasters without negotiating.

steps.title: Walk the Marina
steps.detail: Coffee-fueled waterfront walk from Fort Mason along the Marina Green. Clear your head.

steps.title: Exploratorium or a Bookstore
steps.detail: Head to Pier 15 for the Exploratorium or find a cozy corner at a neighborhood cafe with a book. A very good solo Saturday.

solo.title: Intense Music Thursday
solo.tagline: Go alone, go heavy, feel something.

steps.title: Early Dinner at Bayview Oyster Bar
steps.detail: Start the evening with oysters and Louisiana-Bay Area fusion at the new spot on Third St. Eating at the bar solo is always the right call.

steps.title: Doors at GAMH
steps.detail: Head to the Great American Music Hall for Russian Circles and Primitive Man. $30 advance. Arrive early for a good spot.

steps.title: Let the Music Hit
steps.detail: Post-metal and doom in a gorgeous historic room. No conversation necessary. This is what Thursday nights are for.

birthday.title: Birthday Night Market Crawl
birthday.tagline: Two free night markets on the same Friday. The city is basically throwing you a party.

steps.title: Start at Fort Mason Night Market
steps.detail: Kick off the birthday at the Fort Mason Night Market. Free food vendors, waterfront, and the whole group is happy.

steps.title: Roll to Thrive City
steps.detail: Head to the Dirtybird Night Market for DJ sets, games, and cocktails. The birthday person gets to pick the vibe.

steps.title: Keep Going
steps.detail: The city is yours at this point. SoMa clubs, a bar crawl, wherever the group wants to land.

birthday.title: Punk Birthday at the Fillmore
birthday.tagline: The Damned on their farewell tour is a legitimately legendary birthday story.

steps.title: Pre-Show Dinner
steps.detail: Pick a Hayes Valley spot near Bill Graham or the Fillmore for a group dinner. Keep it casual.

steps.title: Drinks Before the Show
steps.detail: Get to the Fillmore early and grab drinks at the bar. The venue itself is worth showing up for.

steps.title: The Damned Live
steps.detail: Watch one of the original UK punk bands on their 50-year farewell tour. This is a birthday you will actually talk about.

birthday.title: Warriors Game Night
birthday.tagline: Chase Center, courtside energy, and the whole crew together.

steps.title: Pre-Game Arrivals
steps.detail: Get the group together early and explore the new local Bay Area food lineup at Chase Center. The arena food is genuinely worth arriving for.

steps.title: Warriors vs. Magic
steps.detail: Golden State hosts Orlando in a Saturday evening game. The energy in that building is unmatched for a birthday group.

steps.title: Celebrate After
steps.detail: Head to Thrive City post-game if Dirtybird is still going, or find a SoMa bar to close out the birthday right.

friends.title: Free Weekend Double Header
friends.tagline: Museum in the morning, coffee in the afternoon, nothing spent.

steps.title: de Young Museum
steps.detail: Free for Bay Area residents Saturday and Sunday thanks to Bank of America Museums on Us. Big enough to roam and argue about art together.

steps.title: Golden Gate Park Walk
steps.detail: Walk from the museum through the park. Find a bench, debrief the morning, enjoy the November light.

steps.title: SF Coffee Festival Afternoon Session
steps.detail: Swing by Fort Mason for the afternoon stretch of the Coffee Festival. $29 each is very reasonable for the amount of coffee involved.

friends.title: Cider Fest and a Concert
friends.tagline: Start the day drinking cider, end it at a show. Perfect Saturday.

steps.title: SF Fall Cider Fest
steps.detail: SPARK Social SF in Mission Bay for the cider festival. Outdoor, 21+, festive, and very fall.

steps.title: Recovery Snacks and Coffee
steps.detail: Find a neighborhood spot nearby to eat something and sober up slightly before the evening.

steps.title: Foy Vance at GAMH
steps.detail: Head to the Great American Music Hall for Foy Vance and a triple bill of folk and soul. The ornate room is a vibe.

friends.title: Coffee, Culture, and a Concert
friends.tagline: A Saturday so good the group chat stays active for a week.

steps.title: SF Coffee Festival Opens
steps.detail: Fort Mason at opening, unlimited samplings, the whole group caffeinated and ready.

steps.title: Asian Art Museum
steps.detail: Head downtown for Ha Chong-Hyun's hemp-cloth paintings and the Kim Minwook wood show. Culture secured.

steps.title: Brandi Carlile
steps.detail: Grammy-winning powerhouse on a Saturday night. Buy tickets now. Her live shows are genuinely transcendent and the kind of thing friend groups still talk about years later.

parents.title: Park and Museum Saturday
parents.tagline: Golden Gate Park is at its most beautiful in November and it costs absolutely nothing.

steps.title: de Young Museum (Free!)
steps.detail: Free for Bay Area residents this weekend. The American art collection is accessible and genuinely impressive.

steps.title: Picnic in the Park
steps.detail: Pack a lunch and find a bench or meadow in Golden Gate Park. November light, relatively uncrowded, very peaceful.

steps.title: Afternoon Stroll
steps.detail: Walk through the Panhandle or down to Ocean Beach. A slow, relaxed, lovely afternoon.

parents.title: Coffee Festival and a Nice Lunch
parents.tagline: Fort Mason, good coffee, and a proper sit-down lunch. Very civilized.

steps.title: SF Coffee Festival
steps.detail: Fort Mason Festival Pavilion for the 10th Annual. $29 each, unlimited samplings, and the setting is beautiful. Arrive early before the lines build.

steps.title: Lunch in the Marina
steps.detail: Walk to Chestnut St and try Scout, the new Italian-ish spot, or find a familiar favorite in the neighborhood.

steps.title: Walk the Marina Green
steps.detail: Waterfronts, bay views, and a relaxed afternoon walk. Everything parents visiting SF should see.

parents.title: Opera and a Proper Dinner
parents.tagline: San Francisco Opera at the War Memorial is the kind of evening that feels like a gift.

steps.title: Pre-Opera Dinner
steps.detail: Make a reservation in Hayes Valley near the opera house. RT Bistro is getting excellent buzz this fall.

steps.title: SF Opera: The Marriage of Figaro
steps.detail: Mozart at the War Memorial Opera House from $30 per ticket. The building is as impressive as the performance.

steps.title: Nightcap at Bar Antoine Lounge
steps.detail: End the evening at the Galleria Park Hotel mezzanine bar for a quiet cocktail in a beautiful room. The perfect close to a very good night.
